query: What should I do if my car won't start?
generated_text:
If your car won't start, let's go through some troubleshooting steps to identify the issue. First, check if the dashboard lights come on when you turn the key. If they don't, it's likely that the battery is dead. In this case, you can try jump-starting your car. Make sure to follow the proper jump-starting procedure to avoid any damage to the electrical system.

If the dashboard lights do come on, but the car still won't start, it could be a problem with the starter motor or the fuel delivery system. Listen for any clicking sounds when you turn the key. If you hear a clicking sound, it could indicate a faulty starter motor. If you don't hear any sounds, it might be a fuel delivery issue, such as a faulty fuel pump or a clogged fuel filter.

It's also possible that there's an issue with the ignition system, such as a faulty spark plug or a malfunctioning ignition coil. In this case, you may need to have a professional mechanic inspect the system to diagnose the problem.

To further troubleshoot, can you tell me if you've noticed any other symptoms, such as strange noises or warning lights on the dashboard? Additionally, have you recently had any maintenance or repairs done on your car that could be related to the issue?
reference_text: If your car won't start, the most common causes are a dead battery, a faulty starter, or an empty fuel tank. First, check if your headlights and interior lights work; if they are dim or dead, your battery is likely the issue. You can try jump-starting it.

query: How do I check my car's oil level?
generated_text:
To check your car's oil level, you'll want to make sure the engine is turned off and the vehicle is parked on a level surface. Locate the oil dipstick, which is usually labeled "Oil" or have an oil can symbol on it. Pull out the dipstick and wipe it clean with a lint-free cloth or paper towel. Insert the dipstick back into the oil reservoir and pull it out again. The dipstick will now be coated with oil, and the oil level will be indicated by the oil's height on the dipstick.

For your 2020 Corolla, the oil dipstick is typically located near the front of the engine, and it may be labeled as "Oil" or have an oil can symbol on it. Be sure to check your owner's manual if you're unsure where the dipstick is located.

When checking the oil level, also take note of the oil's color and consistency. If the oil is dark or dirty, it may be a sign that the oil is due for a change. If you're unsure about the oil level or condition, it's always a good idea to consult with a professional mechanic for advice. Remember to always refer to your owner's manual for specific guidance on checking the oil level for your particular vehicle.
reference_text: To check your oil level, park the car on level ground and wait for the engine to cool down. Pull out the dipstick, wipe it clean with a rag, insert it all the way back in, and then pull it out again. The oil level should be between the 'Full' and 'Add' (or 'F' and 'L') marks.
